_note: What Shige, the vegetable grower of Minamino, says when the farmer talks to him (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items his own answers to a keepsake and to dishes. The birthday lines (winter 18), the close lines from band 4 and the pumpkin lines once his band 5 scene is seen (heart_shige_5) and the dear lines at band 6 once his band 6 scene is (heart_shige_6). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: A day without weeding! The radishes can mind themselves until tomorrow.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nana wants something from every stall. I said one thing. We'll see who wins.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: I put the first sweet potatoes of the year on the moon table. A grower's thank-you.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Good soil, kind rain, and a girl who grows faster than my cucumbers. A fine year.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Back for more advice? Water at dawn, not at noon. That's all I've got.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: If you see Nana by the pond, tell her supper's at six. She never hears me.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: You're the one who took over the old farm! Shige. I grow greens down here, for the store and the teahouse.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Fellow grower, eh? If your leaves yellow, come ask. Soil talks, if you know how to listen.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Rain! Saves me forty trips to the well. I'm fixing hoe handles today.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Turnips first, always. Quick to grow, quick to sell, and the slugs like them less.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Cucumbers want water morning and night in this heat. And a stick to climb.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Crows got my tomatoes again. Nana says we should make a scarecrow that looks like me.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Daikon's in. Kiku will want some for her pickles. She always does.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nothing grows now but plans. I spend the evenings deciding next year's rows.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: My wife planted those gardens. I just keep them the way she liked. Nana helps.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Sayo buys my greens every morning. Says they're the only ones that don't wilt by noon.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The little shrine by the lane is for the water. Kiku keeps it. Good to bow when you pass.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Horsetail comes up along the lane down to the river before my turnips are even in. Nana picks it by the fistful.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The mulberries are ripe out at the east end of the track and up in the corner past it. Nana's been at them. I can tell by her shirts.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nameko on the old wood by the pines down south. Mushrooms don't need me at all. Humbling, for a grower.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nothing wild down here now but enoki by the pine past my lower beds. Up in Kaminoda the dropwort keeps on at the paddy edges, Genzo says.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nana hid my hoe. 'No work on your birthday, Papa.' So I'm walking the beds with empty hands, planting next year in my head.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: For my birthday? Nana told you, didn't she. ...Well. Thank you. I'll keep it where I can see it from my chair.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Your rows run straighter than they did in spring. I noticed. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nana asks after you at supper. So do I, if I'm honest. How's your soil holding up?

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: I've cleared a spot by the fence for her old seed. Nana checks it every morning, as if it might sprout overnight.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: I'll simmer the first pumpkin her way, sweet. Far too sweet for me. I'll eat the whole pot anyway.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The tin is full again. First time in nine years. I keep lifting the lid just to hear the seeds rattle.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nana wants a pumpkin lantern next fall. I said faces are for scarecrows. She said that's exactly the point.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: I walk out to the fence every dusk now. Not for the vines. Just to stand where she stood. It's an easier standing than it used to be.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Now that's a fine one! I can't grow these as well as you. Teach me sometime.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Thanks! This'll go in tonight's pot.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Oh, for me? Thank you.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Ah, that's more Nana's sort of thing. I'll pass it on.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: A stone? I dig hundreds of those out of the beds each spring. No thank you.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: One's plenty for today. Don't spoil us.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: A moon lantern! Nana's mother used to hang one every fall. ...Thank you. Truly.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Hearty and hot! Nana and I will fight over this one.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: A cooked dish! Saves me burning supper again. Thanks.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Oh, a dish. Thanks, we'll have it tonight.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Too sweet for me. Nana will be thrilled, though.
